title: Experience, Review And Share
objective: Attend an actual arts experience as an audience member, review its artistic qualities and creative impact, and share the final review with another person with evidence.

blocks.text: Silver · Unit 1 · Part 1C · Experience, review and share.
We will learn to notice artistic choices, form a supported view and communicate it. Part 1C needs a real audience experience, your own review, and evidence that you shared that review.
Check EVENT_SLOT for the current arrangement. If it is empty or unconfirmed, today’s work is preparation. A practice review does not show that you attended an experience.
When the experience is arranged, use these steps before and after it. You can record your response through speech, writing, drawing with labels, or another clear format.

This deck directly evidences Silver Unit 1 Part 1C, Review arts events. Source of award requirements: tools/artsaward/SPEC.json, Silver and universal rules. Silver is the Level 2 Award in the Arts, with TWO units evidenced separately. Mark parts P / A / N. ONE Attempted allowed PER UNIT. Any Not Attempted = Below Pass. Results are Pass / Below Pass only. The 20-file cap applies across the whole Silver portfolio, not per unit or lesson. Keep both units and all parts separately identifiable. Nine cumulative part files or two unit files with part sections are optional layouts, not award requirements. Every locator names the actual file plus page, slide or timecode. The four assessment areas are art form knowledge and understanding, creativity, planning and review, and communication. Only an adviser trained at Silver may assess. Delivery is through a validated centre; staff must confirm both conditions, which this deck does not assert are met. Advisers must not write plans, reviews or evidence for pupils. Read, prompt or scribe the pupil’s exact words and check them back without improving them. Core, Extend and Challenge vary support within Silver; each retains the full evidence meaning and the pupil’s own choices. Keep adult models and source quotations distinct from the pupil’s evidence. No forced private disclosure, public performance, filming or posting. Fourteen forty-minute lesson spines do not deliver the whole 95-hour programme; record actual additional guided and independent work.

Silver Unit 1 Part 1C requires at least one arts event or experience attended AS AN AUDIENCE MEMBER, a review of artistic qualities and creative impact, and the review SHARED, evidenced. The serving deck reads EVENT_SLOT through the shared SLOTS.json reader. Check its actual contents: no arrangement is asserted. Support R1 pupils visit, R2 the experience comes in, or R3 live remote delivery. Use the arrival, starter and first model for preparation; after the first We Do, pause for the actual audience experience in recorded programme time, then resume at I Do 2. The experience is not limited to a slide’s minutes. If it has already happened, use the pupil’s actual record. If not arranged, keep all later practice labelled rehearsal and schedule actual attendance, review and final sharing. Desk research, archives and prerecorded video used here are preparation only. Arrange an accessible viewing/listening position and willing review recipient. Optional photos must follow setting consent rules; a factual attendance record and located review can provide evidence without filming faces.

stages.title: Arrival · retrieve

blocks.text: Think about how artists use a choice to shape a work. In visual art, this could be colour, texture, size or space. In a performance, it could be rhythm, pace, movement or voice.
Choose a feature you would like to notice as an audience member. Write a question such as: How does the use of space guide my attention? Keep it open so the work can surprise you.
Look at the shared event information with an adult. Separate what is confirmed from what still needs arranging. Record the actual event title and route only when they are known.
Agree how to keep notes without missing the work itself. A sketch after looking or a spoken note afterwards can help you recall a detail. Use only methods allowed at the experience.

stages.data-ta1: Read the live EVENT_SLOT state. Accept questions in accessible forms. A slot title is preparation information, not proof of attendance or a booking made by this deck.

stages.title: Starter · create the need

blocks.text: Compare these two review notes. First: I liked it. Second: The repeated shapes led my eye towards the large circle, which made that part feel important.
The first note gives a view, but we cannot tell what supports it. The second links a feature to an effect. That link helps another person understand the reviewer’s response.
An artistic quality is something about how the work is made or performed. Creative impact is what its choices make you think, feel, notice or want to try in your own art.
Your impact can differ from someone else’s. You do not need a dramatic feeling. Noticing a new way to arrange shapes can be a useful response to explain.

stages.data-ta1: Treat both notes as invented teaching examples, not evidence of a real event. Keep discussion on responses to the work without inviting personal history.

stages.title: I Do · model

blocks.text: Watch how I turn an observation into a review point. For this practice only, I arrange three small paper squares beside one large circle. This simple display models a method; it is not your audience experience.
I first describe what is there: three small squares lead towards a large circle. I name the artistic choice as scale and placement. I can point to the size change and the gap.
Then I judge the effect: the larger shape draws my attention. I give a reason based on the display. Finally, I explain an impact: it makes me want to test a larger focal shape in a collage.

blocks.title: Build a review from a noticed detail
blocks.caption: A clear example supports your own response.
blocks.alt: NOTICE: point to a detail. NAME: identify an art choice. JUDGE: explain its effect. CONNECT: say its impact on you. A clear example supports your own response.

blocks.text: I could also find a choice less effective. I would still identify the feature and explain why. A review can include praise, doubt or mixed views without guessing what the artist intended.
Keep the model separate from your notes. At the actual experience, gather your own observations as an audience member and retain the original record.

stages.data-ta1: Make the stated simple display in front of pupils; do not refer to an unseen image. Model the observation-to-judgement link before independent review writing. Do not count this demonstration as 1C attendance.

stages.title: We Do · everyone commits

data.heading: Spot an unsupported review claim
data.instruction: Spot the error in these practice claims. Choose a repair that keeps a real artistic example, your own view and the evidence of sharing distinct.

items.label: “I noticed the slow opening pace. That proves the whole audience wanted to make art.”
items.feedback: Your observation can support your own account of an artistic effect. It does not establish everyone else’s creative response.

options.label: Describe your own response and the observed detail.
Keep the whole-audience claim because it sounds positive.

items.label: “My final review is saved in a folder, so another person has received it.”
items.feedback: Saving and sharing are different actions. Record a recipient and evidence only after the final review has actually been communicated.

options.label: A saved filename proves the review was shared.
Keep sharing open until someone actually receives the review.

items.label: “It was good because it was good” is the complete review.
items.feedback: Add a real artistic feature, its effect and your own creative impact. Your judgement may be positive, mixed or critical.

options.label: Use a specific artistic example and explain its impact on you.
Repeat the same judgement in a longer sentence.

data.discussion: At the actual arts experience, attend as an audience member through the agreed access route. Use real notes for your final review and its actual share. If the experience has not happened, label this preparation.

stages.data-ta1: Read the actual prompt and choices; support the pupil to commit before checking. Use the item feedback as a model reason, not a judgement on personal taste. Keep real trials, meetings, views and project actions separate from these teaching examples.

stages.title: I Do 2 · connect

blocks.text: After the real experience, a review and its sharing record have different jobs. Your review communicates what you thought about the work. The sharing record shows that someone actually received that review.

blocks.title: Keep the review and the real share

boxes.head: SHARING RECORD
boxes.line2: how and where it is kept

blocks.caption: A draft swap alone does not evidence the final share.
blocks.alt: MY REVIEW: art choices and examples, my view and creative impact. SHARING RECORD: who received the review, how and where it is kept. A draft swap alone does not evidence the final share.

blocks.text: I model the check without inventing a recipient. Before sharing, I have only a draft and a plan to share. After I communicate the final review, I can record the person or role, the method and the evidence location.

If I read my review to a willing adult, a factual record can say what was shared and how. If I send an agreed digital copy, I keep evidence of that real action. A promise to send it later remains a next step.
Keep your original observations when you shape the final review. They help you check that your examples match the work you experienced.

stages.data-ta1: Show a blank sharing record with who, how and locator fields, filling only real facts after an actual share. Model appropriate methods without sending messages or asserting recipients.

stages.title: We Do 2 · lab

blocks.text: Use your actual experience notes to test a review point with a partner or adult. Identify the work or moment, name an artistic quality, and explain its effect. Then add your own creative impact.
The listener points to the part they can follow and asks about a missing link. Use that question to refine your words. Keep this exchange labelled draft feedback.
Check the event title, the maker or company where known, and the record of attendance. If the experience has not happened, practise with the model and label the whole account preparation.

stages.data-ta1: This lab improves the draft; it is not silently counted as the required final share. Use actual work notes for post-experience pupils and clearly labelled model practice for others.

stages.title: Independent · evidence

blocks.text: Make your final review from the real experience. Include the artistic qualities you noticed and their creative impact on you, using clear examples. Keep your own view, even when someone else disagrees.
Now share your review with a willing person through your chosen method. Record who received it, how you shared it, and where the evidence of that action is saved.

items: Core: use prompts, a reader or an exact scribe. Attend the real experience, make your own review of artistic qualities and creative impact, then actually share it and keep the sharing evidence.
Extend: organise the same attendance record, supported review and evidenced final share in your own format.
Challenge: retain the same attendance, review and sharing evidence; weigh two artistic choices and explain how their effects shape your overall view.

blocks.text: You may speak privately, show a labelled visual review or use an agreed digital form. A long performance is not required. Check that the person receives the finished review, not only a request to hear it later.

stages.data-ta1: Ensure each route includes actual audience attendance, a review covering both required areas, and evidenced final sharing. Scribe only exact pupil words. If attendance or sharing is pending, preserve completed work and arrange the missing action; do not claim a pass from preparation.

stages.title: Exit · check the trail

blocks.text: Find the audience record, the review and the record of its final share. Can a reader tell which arts experience you attended and what you communicated about it?
Save them under Silver Unit 1 Part 1C. Use the actual file name plus page, slide or timecode for each item. Keep the receiver’s name or agreed role and the sharing method with its evidence.
If an action is still missing, name it honestly. If all actions happened, point to a review idea that might influence your own arts practice. Keep that connection in your own words.

stages.data-ta1: Verify actual locators and completed actions. Append within the chosen cumulative unit/part structure and whole-Silver cap. A folder check is not evidence that an absent event or share happened.
